subject.title: [Feature]: Expose per-run token usage on the WebSocket lifecycle event stream

question: Should OpenClaw add public per-run usage data to the Gateway WebSocket stream, and should it be a lifecycle usage phase or a separate run-status event family?
rationale: This affects the stable Gateway RPC/events surface and third-party clients, while current workarounds require polling sessions.usage after lifecycle end with race handling.

options.title: Add a documented usage event
options.body: Define an additive usage event or lifecycle phase with explicit schema, timing, permissions, and tests across the main run paths.

options.title: Use a broader run-status event
options.body: Fold usage into a new documented run-status event family if maintainers want one observability contract for start, progress, terminal state, and usage.

options.title: Keep RPC polling as the contract
options.body: Decline the WebSocket event and document sessions.usage/session-message polling as the supported integration path, accepting the extra client complexity.

recommendation.title: Add a documented usage event
recommendation.body: Define an additive usage event or lifecycle phase with explicit schema, timing, permissions, and tests across the main run paths.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is ownership of the agent event and Gateway lifecycle/control-channel surface that would carry the new contract.
